chunks: Saying: 'Alas the woe, we were iniquitous.'

key_terms.طَاغِينَ: Transgressors, those who exceeded bounds in disbelief or disobedience

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Yaa Waylana' signify in the Quran regarding the regret of sinners?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Qalam (43) is often linked with Surah Az-Zukhruf, describing the moment when the disbelievers realize the futility of their arrogance and the reality of their 'taghut' (transgression) against divine guidance. It underscores the theme of 'tadhyil' (regret) which comes too late, emphasizing that acknowledgment of sin without prior action yields no salvation. This reflects the Shia understanding of the transition from worldly denial to hereafterly realization.
